key_insight: Necking in a crosslinked liquid crystal elastomer can nearly fully recover through reverse phase-boundary motion despite substantial mechanical hysteresis.
engineering_relevance: Recoverable strain localization could inform elastomer components that tolerate large, localized deformation with little permanent shape change.
method: Isothermal loading–unloading of a monodomain elastomer perpendicular to its initial director.
Digital image correlation to track low- and high-stretch regions and interface motion.
Nonconvex constitutive modeling with gradient regularization to describe stretch coexistence and finite-width interfaces.
evidence_signal: Digital image correlation shows high-stretch domains shrinking and necked material thickening during unloading; increasing temperature lowers the loading plateau stress but raises the unloading plateau stress within the recoverable-necking regime.
watch_item: Near-complete shape recovery does not imply mechanical reversibility, and the abstract does not establish long-term cyclic durability.
paper_title: Recoverable Necking Enabled by Reverse Phase-Boundary Motion in Liquid Crystal Elastomers
